messages:
jamie: Heads-up — noticed a ~3x spike in fncall schema rejections this morning for the payments route. Quota churn looks correlated; customers are getting charged for retries even when we soft-fall back. Anyone else seeing this?

sasha: I saw the spike too. Looks like most rejects are 'missing required field' from 2 specific models. Sampling shows payloads from the new canary runtime.

miguel: Can you paste a sample? also which metric is spiking? is it validator.reject_count or invoke.rejects.total?

jamie: validator.reject_count (per-model) up. quick sample (redacted):
```
{"tool":"charge_calc","args":{"amount":null,"currency":"USD"}}
```
missing amount triggered strict schema.

tara: That's the canary that enabled strict tool schema enforcement yesterday. We rolled it to 10% but the routing policy might be sending a higher fraction for low-latency nodes.

sasha: Ah — routing policy 'latency-first' routes to canary in region-eu-west for small seqlen. Need to check overlap with customers on trial pricing.

miguel: Two quick fixes: 1) revert strict enforcement on that canary, or 2) enable soft-validate with audit logging so we accept and surface telemetry. Which do we prefer?

jamie: Prefer soft-validate + audited telemetry so we don't regress behavior while we investigate. But we need to avoid charging for retries when soft-validate triggers fallback. Right now billing hooks count any invoke as billable.

tara: Agreed on soft-validate. Ops: is it feasible to tag fallbacks in the billing pipeline so they are zero-rated?

ops-bot: @billing team notified: invoice-exceptions created for trace_ids matching this thread.

miguel: For telemetry, can we add a sampled payload store for rejects (PII redacted) with rate limit e.g., 1 per 1000 rejects per customer, and a path to view in console under 'Validator -> Samples'? That helps triage without storing everything.

sasha: +1. We should also emit a validator.reason label (enum: missing_field, type_mismatch, extra_field) and a model_variant tag so dashboards can pivot.

jamie: UX ask: in Console > Rollouts, show active validators and their strictness level per slice (percent, regions). Right now rollout UI only shows traffic percent.

tara: That'd be useful. We can reuse the existing rollout matrix and add a 'validation profile' column. Low effort?

miguel: Backend needs to surface validator config to the control-plane API; small change. But we must be careful about exposing internal validator names to customers. Use friendly IDs.

sasha: Also need a sampling heuristic: prioritize samples from customers hitting quota errors and from first-party integration tests. Otherwise noise will drown out root causes.

jamie: One more: for soft-validate, we should emit a trace span `validator.soft_accept` with metadata: original_payload_hash, redacted_payload_sample_id, fallback_model. That will link errors->billing->traces.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: rollout/validator-softmode -> canary (10%) at 2623456900 per @tara

tara: I'll hold the canary until billing tagging and sampling are in place. ETA for infra changes ~4h.

miguel: I'll put a temporary dashboard tile: "validator.reject_rate (canary)" + dimension by model_variant. Also add an alert if reject_rate > 1% and correlated fallback_count rises.

sasha: Let's also add a one-click action in the console to flip validator to soft for a specific slice (region/model/percent). Saves manual deploys.

jamie: Sounds good. For the billing side, I'll coordinate with finance to zero-rate retries in the piping for incidents caused by validator-mode changes.

tara: Will update the rollout PR with a flag `soft_validate=true` and an annotation field for retention_policy on samples.

jamie: Thanks everyone. Action items: miguel -> dashboard tile & alert, tara -> infra + rollout PR w/ sample retention, sasha -> sampling heuristic + reason tags, miguel & jamie -> link traces to billing. I'll keep thread open. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: incident stub created INC-2026-142 for monitoring and billing follow-up.
